answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, causing influence to decay across weakly connected regions. A sybil cluster forms a sparse external cut with low conductance φ; conductance and min-cut transitivity bounds limit the probability that walks enter or persist within it, thereby bounding its aggregate voting weight. A mirror, opal, or raven identity cannot bypass this constraint without credible cross-cluster attestations.
